easy.explanation: Psalm 24:1 says, “The earth is the LORD’S... the world, and they that dwell therein.”
easy.q: To whom do the earth, the world, and those who dwell therein belong?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says that He “hath founded it upon the seas.”
easy.q: Upon what did the LORD found the earth?

answers: Only those who dwell on the earth
The earth, the world, and those who dwell therein
easy.explanation: The verse includes the earth, the world, and all who dwell therein.
easy.q: Who is included among those belonging to the LORD in verse 1?

answers: Verse 2 explains how the LORD founded and established the earth
Verse 2 describes a person with clean hands
medium.explanation: Verse 1 declares the LORD’s ownership of the world, while verse 2 describes how He founded and established it.
In this verse, “the world” refers to the earth and its inhabitants.
medium.q: In the phrase “the world, and they that dwell therein,” what does “the world” refer to?

answers: The world is under the LORD’s rule
The world belongs only to its inhabitants
The seas have no connection with the earth
medium.explanation: The LORD’s ownership and founding of the earth express His sovereignty over creation.
medium.q: What can be understood from the fact that the earth belongs to the LORD and was founded by Him?

answers: The world exists without a foundation
The LORD owns the world and founded it
Only the rivers belong to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verses present both the LORD’s ownership of the world and His work in founding and establishing it.
challenge.q: What central idea is developed by these two verses together?

answers: Because people also belong to the world that is His
challenge.explanation: The verse speaks not only of the earth but also of all its inhabitants.
challenge.q: Why does mentioning those who dwell in the world strengthen the idea of the LORD’s kingship?

challenge.explanation: The passage says that He “hath founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the floods.”
challenge.q: Which pair of actions describes the LORD’s work toward the earth?

answers: He that hath clean hands and a pure heart
easy.explanation: Verse 4 describes the worthy person as one with “clean hands, and a pure heart.”
easy.q: Who may ascend into the hill of the LORD?

answers: As one who has not lifted up his soul unto vanity
As one who seeks the gates
easy.explanation: The person has not lifted up his soul unto vanity and has not sworn deceitfully.
easy.q: How is the person worthy to stand in the LORD’s holy place described?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 speaks of those “that seek him, that seek thy face.”
easy.q: What does the generation described in verse 6 seek?

answers: One describes clean actions and the other describes inner purity
One describes the seas and the other the floods
medium.explanation: The verse joins outward conduct, represented by clean hands, with inward character, represented by a pure heart.
medium.q: How are “clean hands” and “a pure heart” related?

answers: In a dishonest or deceptive manner
medium.explanation: To swear deceitfully is to make a dishonest or deceptive oath.
medium.q: What does “deceitfully” mean in the phrase “nor sworn deceitfully”?

answers: A blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation
A key to the everlasting doors
medium.explanation: Verse 5 says, “He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.”
medium.q: What does the person described in verses 4–5 receive?

answers: Those who seek the LORD’s face are described as clean and upright
Seeking the LORD’s face replaces the need for honesty
There is no connection between the two ideas
challenge.explanation: The generation seeking the LORD’s face follows the description of the person who is pure and truthful.
challenge.q: What connection is made between purity of life and seeking the LORD’s face?

challenge.explanation: “Nor sworn deceitfully” directly concerns honesty in making an oath.
challenge.q: Which phrase in verse 4 emphasizes honesty in speech?

answers: A question about who is worthy, a description of his character, and then the blessing he receives
A description of the gates, followed by the floods, and then a battle
The blessing is presented before the person is described
challenge.explanation: The passage first asks who may approach, then describes that person, and finally states what he receives.

paragraphs.title: The Entrance of the King of Glory

answers: For the entrance of the King of glory
For a person to ascend the hill
For the founding of the earth
easy.explanation: The gates are told to rise because “the King of glory shall come in.”
easy.q: Why are the gates commanded to lift up and open?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 calls Him “the LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 8?

answers: Those who dwell in the world
easy.explanation: Verse 10 declares, “The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory.”
easy.q: Who is the King of glory according to the final verse?

answers: Lift up their heads and open
medium.explanation: The passage repeats the command, “Lift up your heads, O ye gates,” and speaks of the everlasting doors being lifted up.
medium.q: What are the gates commanded to do?

medium.explanation: In this context, “strong” describes the LORD’s power and might.
medium.q: What does “strong” convey in the description “The LORD strong and mighty”?

medium.explanation: Verse 10 identifies the King of glory as “the LORD of hosts.”
medium.q: What additional title for the LORD appears in verse 10?

answers: To emphasize preparation for the entrance of the King of glory
To show that the gates belong to human beings
To replace the description of the LORD’s power
challenge.explanation: The repeated call highlights the opening of the gates for the King of glory.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of repeating the call to the gates in verses 7 and 9?

answers: Both emphasize the LORD’s power and rule
Both describe the purity of a person
Both describe how the earth was founded
challenge.explanation: Both titles present the LORD as powerful and sovereign over His hosts.
challenge.q: What connection exists between “mighty in battle” and “the LORD of hosts”?

answers: From strength and might to the title “the LORD of hosts”
From clean hands to seeking the LORD’s face
From seas and floods to founding the earth
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes the LORD’s strength and might, then identifies Him as the LORD of hosts and the King of glory.
challenge.q: How does the description of the King of glory develop in verses 8–10?
